chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

“When you see the crescent, then fast; and when you see it, then break the fast. It is not by opinion or conjecture. And sighting is not that ten people stand looking, then one of them says, ‘There it is, there it is,’ while nine look and do not see it. Rather, when one sees it, a thousand see it.”

key_terms.أَلْفٌ: a thousand, expressing broad and clear visibility
key_terms.الْهِلَالَ: the crescent moon marking the start or end of the fasting month
key_terms.بِالرَّأْيِ: by personal opinion rather than established sighting
key_terms.فَأَفْطِرُوا: then break the fast upon confirmed sighting
key_terms.فَصُومُوا: then begin fasting upon confirmed sighting
key_terms.يَنْظُرُونَ: they look attentively for the moon

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the rule for fasting and breaking the fast upon sighting the crescent?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the beginning and ending of the fast are tied to actual sighting of the crescent moon. It rejects relying on mere opinion and conjecture, and emphasizes a clear, credible sighting rather than an isolated claim contradicted by others present.
